2609.21231.title: Beyond Reference-Based Evaluation: Reward Models for Meta-Evaluation of Grammatical Error Correction
2609.21231.paper_summary: Reference-based metrics for Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) such as M$^2$ and ERRANT assume that the reference set enumerates all valid edits, and therefore often penalize corrections that are grammatical and meaning-preserving but phrased differently. We introduce RM-EVAL, a reward model trained on human preference data from SEEDA, as a reference-free meta-evaluator that predicts human-like quality judgments at both full-sequence and partial-sequence levels. Beyond evaluation, we show that the same reward model can be used as a learning signal to improve GEC generation via Reward-Guided Text Generation (RGTG), which keeps a base GEC model frozen and performs online, reward-driven decoding. Across SEEDA, RM-EVAL achieves strong agreement with human rankings, and RGTG yields consistent gains in reward and external validation, demonstrating a unified framework for both assessing and enhancing GEC systems without relying on gold references.
2609.21231.paper_summary_zh: 參考基礎的語法錯誤修正（GEC）指標，如 M$^2$ 和 ERRANT，假設參考集列舉了所有有效的編輯，因此經常會對那些語法正確且保留意義但措辭不同的修正進行懲罰。我們引入 RM-EVAL，一種基於人類偏好數據訓練的獎勵模型，作為一種無參考的元評估器，能夠在完整序列和部分序列層面預測類人質量判斷。除了評估之外，我們展示了相同的獎勵模型可以作為學習信號，通過獎勵引導文本生成（RGTG）來改善 GEC 生成，這一過程保持基礎 GEC 模型不變，並進行在線的、以獎勵為驅動的解碼。在 SEEDA 中，RM-EVAL 與人類排名達成強一致性，而 RGTG 在獎勵和外部驗證上均帶來一致的增益，展示了一個統一的框架，用於評估和增強 GEC 系統，而無需依賴黃金參考。
